findings.failure_mode: A deploy reports success, but some tasks are silently missing from the new worker. Triggers for those tasks then fail with task-not-found or run against stale metadata, and the only trace is an error log line.
findings.trigger_condition: A transient DB error or timeout, a unique-constraint race, or a queue-creation failure occurs for one task while the worker's tasks are registered.
findings.amplifier: createWorkerTask catches every non-validation error and returns null. createWorkerTasks drops null entries with `if (entry)`, so the worker is finalized with a partial task set. The 3-attempt createMany loop only covers duplicate conflicts, not other errors.
findings.sustaining_effect: The partial worker is the current worker until the next deploy. Re-deploys of an unchanged build may skip the task again, so the gap persists.
findings.blast_radius: Every trigger of the dropped tasks in that environment fails until a redeploy succeeds. Other tasks in the worker are unaffected.

evidence.note: catch logs the error and returns null for all non-validation errors
null entries are skipped with no count check or throw
changed the task-registration conflict handling in this function

findings.confidence_rationale: The swallow-and-drop path is plain in the code, but I did not observe a production partial registration. The cited commit is a [feature], not a [fix].
findings.how_to_verify: Make backgroundWorkerTask.createMany throw a non-validation error for one task in a 5-task deploy. Check whether the deploy succeeds with 4 task entries and no error returned to the CLI.

notes: Rejected the S08 findMany leads (scoped per worker or environment; I did not read them in depth). Rejected the S10 lead: the retryConfig at line 676 is stored task config, not a retry layer. The S06 lead is a plain lookup in an in-memory array.
